reviews.comment: Dr. Kallendorf was one of the best professors I had the honor of learning from. He was always available to offer help outside of class. I worked with him on an independent research paper later on in my undergrad years, and I still have his feedback to this day. A fantastic lecturer and a caring professor. I will miss him.

This class can be intimidating at first if u are unfamiliar w/ older periods & texts, but that was the beauty of the course, for I learned so much! He taught something I wasn't familiar with, & he did a great job teaching in that I feel much more knowledgeable afterwards. He has great current examples that we can relate to which was sweet. Loved!

This class and Professor Kallendorf are amazing. I didn't do the readings, I just showed up to class and paid attention and I was fine. The material was really interesting and Professor Kallendorf was very knowledgeable about it. All of the grades are based on tests and a final paper. I would definitely recommend taking this class if you can!

I went to most classes and study more for this class than any of my others. He is a very tough grader. There two essay questions each exam and I would write over two pages for each one and still never received an A+. This class is a hard A and I would not recommend if you have a moderate to heavy workload.

Dr. Kallendorf is a nice guy with a good sense of humor, and he was definitely helpful when giving feedback. This class is pretty tough though. Daily homework and participation that can be somewhat time consuming, and very labor-intensive tests that can be really challenging
Dr. Kallendorf is an awesome guy to work with. He made my last semester of Latin amazing! Definitely recommend...

He is a lot of fun to listen to, but his lectures are dense and reading heavy. Your grade is determined by three essay exams and a term paper. Make sure to write well with proper grammar as he is an English professor and grades hard on mechanics.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I bought the textbook, but didn't really use it. I used sparknotes for a lot of the readings but even so he goes over everything in class so if you attend the lectures you don't really need to read/study hard. He's really engaging and prioritizes discussion. Really genuine teaching style.

ENGL 219 with Kallendorf is a fantastic call for an english credit. It has been pretty easy. He cares about you learning and offered zoom sessions that show exactly what he wants you to know for the exams. It is very clear what you have to read in week folders and I didn't use any textbook and got an A every time.
Lovely class and professor! I never read the readings just the outlines and attended lectures and got an A. Really fun topic and learned a lot! Take this class you won't regret it!!
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Kallendorf has given up on verbally teaching. With the switch to online classes, he only gave only one 15 min zoom meeting prior to taking the first Exam. He expects you to learn on your own and gives very little guidance. With his refusal to verbally teach and his harsh grading, I see no possibility of receiving an A. Very disappointed.

This professor was really hard to read. He grades by four essays, and while some say he's an easy grader, I always felt he went a lot harder than what other profs expected. He has a super old school way of teaching which didn't work for me. I'm not sure what I did wrong in this class, but it wasn't as easy of an A that I was told it was.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Kallendorf is probably my favorite professor!! He's dorky & tries to make class interesting & fun. He wants everyone to do good so he gives out reviews, outlines and has a review class before the test! There isn't attendance but he knows everyone's names & tries to get people to participate so showing up definitely gets you some brownie points.

He was a great prof. He doesn't take attendance but he doesn't post lectures and it'll be hard to get an A if you miss a lot. Fairly easy grader, 3 essay tests and one paper. DON'T buy the book! it was barely used and you can already find all the old plays/documents online for free. Lighthearted and I would take again
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I loved this class and Kallendorf! It's an easy A w/ 3 essay tests and a final paper, but he gives in class reviews, review sheets, and posts outlines that are pretty straightforward for every topic covered so you know exactly what to write for the tests + paper. His lectures are very interesting and he's also a very lenient grader + super nice!!!

Dr. Kallendorf's class is pretty straightforward and enjoyable for someone who likes reading and art. His lectures are interesting, and he's a nice guy, but he does have a tendency to insert his own views as a baseline for discussion a bit much. Tests are essay-based, but he's a generous grader, so don't worry too much if writing isn't your thing

Dr. Kallendorf is one of my favorite professors I've had at A&M so far. He's such a great guy. He's a lovable mega-nerd & will be goofy in class which makes the lectures even more interesting. He gives great feedback on tests and really appreciates original thought processes. If you read, this class can be an easy A and is definitely worth taking.

Dr. Kallendorf cares about whether students do well in his class, attendance isn't mandatory, but he will go over topics that make the essay tests way easier! All grades are essays, but graded fairly and without bias. My favorite professor at A&M, 10/10 would take again!
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Dr. Kallendorf might be the nicest man alive, didn't make the class any easier, but it did make it more enjoyable. He really has a fascination with rhetoric and a drive to help his students understand the material. All the tests were timed in class essays, so be prepared to study. Very conceptual and ideologically based course. No homework.

I enjoy the subject, so I might be biased but I loved this class so much I declared an English minor! Tests are in essay form but he leaves his questions pretty open ended so it's not hard. If you take good notes to look back on you'll be fine. He really takes into account anything you say and will work with you.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures
